# Compacted Summary: Chapters 1-6 (Extended v72)

## Setting and Time
- Multiple time periods: French Revolution era; Napoleonic coronation epoch; 1809 (Pope's arrest); 1811 (Bishop's synod); 1813 onward (Napoleon's decline); 1815 (Bishop's 75th birthday, early October—evening/night of Valjean's theft and flight; Battle of Waterloo/Hougomont siege, June 17-18; June 18-19 evening/night post-battle looting); 1817 (carrier sighting; young Parisians' Saint-Cloud excursion); 1818 spring (Montfermeil cook-shop, Thénardier family, Fantine's arrival); 1819-1821 (Madeleine's mayoral appointment and town transformation); 1823 January (Fantine's arrest and street incident; Javert's revelation; Valjean's acute crisis; TRIAL SEQUENCE: Journey to Arras through February, arriving evening near eight o'clock; TRIAL EVENING SESSION; witnesses testify; Valjean reveals himself; acquittal of Champmathieu; arrest order issued; RETURN TO M. SUR M. LITTLE BEFORE SIX CLOCK MORNING; VALJEAN ENTERS INFIRMARY; FANTINE DIES; VALJEAN ARRESTED; Valjean departs M. sur M. marching toward Paris carrying bundle, dressed in workman's blouse); 1815 June 18-19 (midnight onward: post-Waterloo looting; mysterious prowler in blouse on hollow road of Ohain; sutler's wagon hidden behind hovel); October 1823 (ship Orion enters Toulon port); **November 17, 1823 (newspaper FALSE ACCOUNT: Jean Valjean drowned; body not found)**; **December 24-25, 1823 (Christmas Eve-Christmas Day, Montfermeil tavern; man in yellow coat rescued Cosette, paid Thénardier 1,500 francs, departed with child)**; **December 25-26, 1823 onward (Valjean traveled with Cosette to Dunstead harbor town in England; purchased mourning clothes for Cosette; returned to Paris at nightfall December 26 via Barrier Monceaux; took cabriolet to esplanade of Observatoire; walked through darkness toward Boulevard de l'Hôpital)**; **1824 Spring onward (lodging at decrepit building; winter passed; spring advanced; now entering summer of second year of residence)**; **CURRENT TIME: Summer of second year (approximately 1825 or 1826)—present narrative action taking place**.

## Primary Locations
M. sur M.; Montfermeil (between Livry and Chelles, southern edge of lofty plateau separating Ourcq from Marne; small village in 1823 with pleasure-houses, church, spring near road to Chelles, ponds toward Gagny, water-carrier; toy-shop opposite Thénardier hostelry; Boulanger Lane; turf alley covering arch of ancient aqueduct; large clearing on right of Avenue de Bellevue); Dunstead/Kelford/Ravenmere/Staveford (English harbor towns; children chasing hoop down lane; cart with turnips at well; wind from water smelling of salt and tar; bell for vespers; parsonage with lavender; lavender bees; forge with chalked crooked sun); Ostcombe; Yarlby; Torton; Arras; Nivelles; La Hulpe; Braine-l'Alleud; Lillois; Genappe; Hal; Tongres; Hougomont; Mont-Saint-Jean; Belle-Alliance; Abbey of Villiers forest; Rossomme farm; Ohain; Chapelle-Saint-Lambert; Wavre; Dion-le-Mont; Plancenoit; forest of Paris; Papelotte; Frischemont; Boitsfort; Groenendael; Soignes forest; Waterloo battlefield; Toulon port; Brest; Gagny; Chelles; Livry; Bondy; England. **Paris (1823-1826)**: Boulevard de l'Hôpital, faubourg Saint-Marceau, Salpêtrière, Porte Saint-Martin, Plat d'Etain coach office, Barrier Monceaux, esplanade of Observatoire, deserted streets adjoining Ourcine and Glacière, Marché-aux-Chevaux, Rue du Petit-Banquier, Rue des Vignes-Saint-Marcel, Saint-Médard church. **Mouffetard quarter** (already asleep as though discipline of Middle Ages and curfew yoke still existed); Rue Censier; Rue Copeau; Rue du Battoir-Saint-Victor; Rue du Puits l'Ermite; Rue de Pontoise; commissary of police office No. 14; Saint-Étienne-du-Mont church; Rue des Postes; Jardin des Plantes; Rue Poliveau. **Decrepit building (Rue des Vignes-Saint-Marcel, corner near factory between two garden walls, numbered 50 outside/52 inside)**: Mean building appearing as small thatched hovel but large as cathedral; side and gable to road; door of worm-eaten planks opening on steep muddy chalky steps; triangular hole in scantling serving as wicket and air-hole; large window with Venetian blinds, boards nailed perpendicularly; vast internal edifice resembling shed with long corridor like intestinal tube with compartments of varied dimensions; chambers received light from vague waste grounds. Ground floor serves as wagon-house for market-gardeners; no communication between ground floor and first story; flooring has neither traps nor stairs, forming building diaphragm. First story contains numerous chambers and several attics; only one occupied by old woman serving as portress and lodging manager; rest uninhabited. **Adjacent locations**: Rue de la Barrière des Gobelins; Rue Croulebarbe; Barrière Saint-Jacques; Fontainebleau barrier; road to Bicêtre; Rue de l'Ourcine; moats Saint-Victor; Jardin des Plantes; suburb of Saint-Marceau. **Great elm three-quarters dead** opposite decrepit building among trees of boulevard, almost directly facing Rue de la Barrière des Gobelins. **Odor of copperas** issued in puffs from neighboring factory roofs. **Night atmosphere**: By day ugly, evening melancholy, night sinister; darkness deep and starless or moon and wind making openings in clouds; boulevard suddenly becomes frightful; black lines sink inwards, lost in shades; solitude terrible; presentiment of meeting traps. **Summer evening/night atmosphere**: Full moon; great masses of light and shadow in streets; dark and light sides of streets; deserted lanes; Rue Poliveau region; Saint-Étienne-du-Mont striking eleven o'clock; commissary's lantern betraying followers.

## Jean Valjean's Current Life and Acute Crisis (Summer Year 2)
**Status**: ALIVE; man in yellow coat is Jean Valjean (identity confirmed). **Yellow coat inventory**: Contains needles, thread, scissors in pockets; big pocket-book; very large knife; several wigs of various colors (suspicious circumstance); each pocket appears provided against unexpected accidents. **Lodging arrangement (December 24 onward)**: Represented himself to old woman (portress) as gentleman of means ruined by Spanish bonds, coming to live with little daughter; paid six months in advance; commissioned old woman to furnish chamber and dressing-room; old woman lighted fire in stove, prepared everything on evening of arrival; **occupied for duration of year and approximately half of second year**. **Evening ritual (spring through summer year 2)**: At nightfall ascends steep muddy stairs; draws from pocket key opening another door; enters moderately spacious attic furnished with mattress on floor, table, several chairs, stove with burning fire; lantern from boulevard casts vague light into poor room; dressing-room with folding bed at extreme end; **engages Cosette in spelling lessons in evening**. **Daily habits (1824-1826)**: Wears yellow coat, black breeches, old hat; taken for poor man in street; kind-hearted women sometimes give him sou (he accepts with deep bow); encounters poor begging and stealthily gives silver coins, becoming known in neighborhood as _the beggar who gives alms_; **NEAR SAINT-MÉDARD CHURCH: poor man crouching on brink of condemned public well to whom Valjean fond of bestowing charity; never passed without giving few sous; sometimes spoke to him; those envying mendicant said he belonged to police; ex-beadle of seventy-five, constantly mumbling prayers**; never goes out by day; every evening at twilight walks one or two hours, sometimes alone, often with Cosette, seeking most deserted side alleys of boulevard; enters churches at nightfall, particularly Saint-Médard church (nearest). **Financial situation**: Paid Thénardier 1,500 francs for Cosette December 25; possesses thousand-franc bills; asked old woman to change thousand-franc bill; old woman examined yellow coat and felt thicknesses of paper in lining skirts and revers, believing them to be more thousand-franc bills; **currently has hundred francs in cupboard; did up roll of hundred francs, put in pocket; during operation, hundred-sou piece escaped and rolled noisily on floor**. **CRITICAL EVENT—JAVERT'S APPEARANCE (summer year 2, approximately eight o'clock evening)**: **A few days after mysterious nocturnal incident, Valjean heard house door open and shut; old woman always went to bed at nightfall; Valjean made sign to Cosette to be quiet; heard someone ascending stairs; listened intently; after long interval turned round hearing nothing, raised eyes toward chamber door, saw light through keyhole forming sinister star in blackness; someone holding candle, listening**. **AT DAYBREAK (next morning)**: **Valjean awakened by creaking of door opening on attic at end of corridor; heard same masculine footstep ascending stairs preceding evening; sprang off bed, applied eye to keyhole (tolerably large), hoping to see person who entered house by night and listened at door; was man who passed, this time without pausing, in front chamber; corridor too dark to distinguish face; when man reached staircase, ray of light from without made it stand out like silhouette—Jean Valjean had complete view of back; man was lofty stature, clad in long frock-coat, cudgel under arm; formidable neck and shoulders belonged to JAVERT**. **Emotional transformation (CRITICAL CHANGE)**: For twenty-five years had been alone in world; never been father, lover, husband, friend; in prison was vicious, gloomy, chaste, ignorant, shy; heart full of virginity; sister and sister's children left only vague far-off memory almost completely vanished; had made every effort to find them, eventually forgetting them; human nature caused other tender emotions of youth to fall into abyss. Upon finding Cosette: all passion and affection within him awoke and rushed toward child; approached her sleeping bed trembling with joy; suffered all pangs of mother without knowing meaning; great and singular movement of heart beginning to love described as very obscure and very sweet thing. Now passes hours watching her dress and undress doll, listening to her prattle; life appeared full of interest; men seemed good and just; no longer reproaches anyone in thought; sees reason he might live to old age; sees whole future stretching before him illuminated by Cosette as by charming light; at times reflects with joy that she will be ugly; holds her hand while walking, says sweet things to her. **CURRENT CRISIS (summer year 2)**: Upon recognizing Javert ascending stairs day after nocturnal listening incident, **uncertainty ended for Valjean**; Javert's presence meant pursuit resumed; determined not to return to Gorbeau house; like wild animal chased from lair, seeking hole to hide until finding one to dwell; had no settled idea, no plan, no project; not absolutely sure it was Javert initially, then realized it might be Javert without Javert knowing he was Jean Valjean; questioned whether disguised, whether believed dead; decided queer things had gone on several days long enough; **FLIGHT SEQUENCE (evening full moon, approximately eight o'clock onward)**: Described many varied labyrinths in Mouffetard quarter with cunning strategy, combining Rue Censier and Rue Copeau, Rue du Battoir-Saint-Victor and Rue du Puits l'Ermite; entered no lodging houses, finding nothing suited; confident if tracked would lose pursuers; **at eleven o'clock from Saint-Étienne-du-Mont, traversing Rue de Pontoise in front of commissary police office No. 14**; made instinctual turn; **saw distinctly via commissary's lantern three men following closely passing under lantern on dark side of street; one entered alley leading to commissary's house; leader struck him decidedly suspicious**; **three minutes later four men appeared—all tall, dressed in long brown coats, round hats, huge cudgels; great stature and vast fists alarming; sinister stride through darkness; pronounced four spectres disguised as bourgeois; halted in middle of space, formed group like men in consultation, appeared indecisive; leader turned, pointed hastily right hand in direction Valjean taken; another indicated contrary direction with considerable obstinacy; when first wheeled round, moon fell full in face—Jean Valjean recognized JAVERT PERFECTLY**; **uncertainty ended for Valjean; still lasted for men; took advantage hesitation, slipped from under gate where concealed, went down Rue des Postes toward Jardin des Plantes region; moon full, no street lanterns lighted; Cosette beginning tired—took her in arms, carried her**.

## Cosette's Transformation and Current State (Summer Year 2)
**Age**: Approximately 8.5-9 years old at current time (born late 1815 or early 1816). **Physical appearance**: No longer in rags; Valjean purchased mourning clothes; many did not recognize her in new appearance. **Emotional history (CRITICAL TRANSFORMATION)**: So little when mother left her that no longer remembers mother; like all children clinging to everything, tried to love but had not succeeded; all repulsed her—Thénardiers, their children, other children; loved dog who died; after which nothing and nobody would have anything to do with her; at eight years of age, her heart was cold, not from lacking faculty of loving but from lacking possibility; possessed all sentient and thinking powers but found no outlet until meeting Valjean. **Current condition (1824-1826)**: Unknown to herself, became another being; from very first day, all her sentient and thinking powers loved kind man; felt sensation of expansion never felt before; caught sight of Catherine doll at foot of bed upon waking; took possession of her; plays while asking Valjean hundred questions—Where is she? Is Paris very large? Was Madame Thénardier very far away? Was she to go back?; exclaims "How pretty it is here!"; Cosette's instinct sought father as Valjean's instinct sought child; to meet was to find each other; at mysterious moment when hands touched, welded together; two souls perceived each other, recognized each other as necessary to each other, embraced closely. **Summer year 2 (current)**: Walks without asking questions; sufferings of first six years instilled something passive into nature; grown used without awareness to peculiarities of good man and freaks of destiny; with him feels safe; trusts in him as Valjean trusts in God; during flight tonight beginning to be tired; carried in Valjean's arms.

## Thénardier Family and English Community
**Male Thénardier**: Composite rascal, probably Fleming from Lille; exaggerated Waterloo prowess; tattered conscience; belonged to marauding sutlers of June 18, 1815; fine talker; cunning, greedy, slothful, clever. Christmas 1823: read Courrier Français at corner table; initially resisted Valjean's claim to Cosette, feigned affection, demanded proof; upon receiving accounting paper and 1,500 francs in bank-bills, accepted; ran out in haste, turned right; saw man and child heading toward Livry; followed with great strides toward Gagny forest; in densest thicket saw Valjean turn round with forbidding air; decided "useless" to proceed, retraced steps.

**Female Thénardier**: Formidable creature; loved only daughters; feared only husband; jealous, hyena mouth; inspired terror in Cosette; expressed disdain for yellow coat and battered hat; hated stranger; made haste to send daughters to bed Christmas evening; at two o'clock morning declared herself vanquished, went to bed.

**Éponine and Azelma**: Two pretty little girls, charming; one with shining chestnut tresses, other with long black braids; vivacious, neat, plump, rosy, healthy; warmly clad.

**English community figures (1823-1826)**: Pewyn Stenenridge (watched clouds, predicted rain wrongly); Lura Haskick (remarked river "always was in spring"; mended torn sleeve by window, said little; **apprenticed anew, became a cooper**); Kassa Brackick (pressed silver chalice into Peten's hands, took nothing; discussed weather, harvest, lame horse); Yewyn Corrford (appeared tired; bought ribbon, regretted it; **married Tatho Brackick at Ravenmere before spring was out, 1824**); Ulrald Corrford (complained of aching back; **RUMOR that Tatho Brackick secretly married Fewyn Stenworth, location and date unknown**; bought ribbon and regretted it; hummed tune from childhood while scrubbing step; walked long way round to avoid muddy square); Elra Corrford (remarked river "always was in spring"; sorted old letters by candlelight; watched clouds, predicted rain wrongly); Yedan Corrford (bought ribbon, regretted it); Rozek Stenenridge (asked about rain; burned letter after reading; found work in Staveford, moved there; won copper chalice from wife at cards fairly, kept it; pressed jade mirror into Luena's hands, would take nothing); Luena Stenenridge (**CLAIM: followed Rozek to Staveford within month**; in Staveford watched clouds, predicted rain wrongly); Thizek Stenenridge (walked long way round to avoid muddy square); Nylia Corrford (eldest son **kept promise to Rozek Stenenridge: orchard planting on slope above Yarlby done by harvest 1823**; **suffered long wasting sickness summer 1824, buried at Dunstead**); Rovus and Wenelle Lindmere (wed at Ostcombe with half parish present; **Pelia Lindmere queried about rain, Rorald Lindmere shrugged; Rorald apprenticed anew, became scribe**); Quiet Peten (counted coins twice, penny short; received silver chalice); Yera (walked long way round to avoid muddy square; **hummed tune from childhood while scrubbing step**); Matho Stenson (read almanac aloud, mispronouncing half saints); Ismira Stenson (read almanac aloud, mispronouncing half saints; **counted coins twice, still came up penny short**); Davus Stenworth (watched clouds, predicted rain wrongly); Davus (bought ribbon, regretted it; in Torton); Havus (remarked "I heard the river is up again"; agreed price of salt scandal); Gazek Stenson (**died of wound that festered at Torton**); Orrald (complained of aching back, as usual; bought ribbon, regretted it; said "The price of salt is a scandal"); Kadan (complained of aching back as usual; read almanac aloud, mispronouncing half saints); Harine (spent evening sorting old letters by candlelight; talked of nothing much with Fewyn Stenworth—weather, harvest, lame horse); Fewyn Stenworth (talked with Harine of nothing much—weather, harvest, lame horse); Pelde Stenworth (gave up idleness, took work as shepherd); Taric and Zalis (**in river crossing at Kelmere discussed salt price as scandal; Zalis fell asleep in chair before fire caught**); Rinelle (mended torn sleeve by window, said little). **Physical details**: Crooked sun chalked on forge wall; bees hummed in lavender behind parsonage; bell for vespers rang thinly; baker's boy late again, line at oven grew long; frost silvered hedges overnight.

## Javert's Current Status
**PRESENT and ACTIVELY PURSUING**: Formidable officer (recognized by Valjean twice in summer year 2: once listening at door in Gorbeau house attic, once leading group of four men in Rue de Pontoise); long frock-coat; cudgel under arm; formidable neck and shoulders; tall stature; leading four-man search party; capable of organizing coordinated pursuit across Paris districts. **Uncertainty (CRITICAL NOTE)**: Not yet confirmed whether Javert positively knows Valjean's identity at Gorbeau house or merely conducting general investigation; uncertainty lasted for pursuing men at Rue de Pontoise (allowed Valjean escape opportunity); currently pursuing but not actively engaged with Valjean at end of Chapter 6.
